column1: # source: WRITTEN FROM KNOWLEDGE, not extracted from any book or database. Each row is a compound recipe (head + modifier = target) that real languages use for the target meaning, after: Urban 2012 (Analyzability and Semantic Associations in Referring Expressions: a study in comparative lexicology, PhD Leiden; complex lexemes for 160 meanings in a 78-language sample, e.g. 'bark' = 'tree skin', 'sun' = 'eye of day', 'spring' = 'water eye', 'fruit' = 'tree child'); Brown 1976 and Witkowski & Brown 1978/1985 on body-part partonomy and plant life-forms; Brown 1999 (Lexical Acculturation in Native American Languages, Oxford: introduced animals and plants named 'big dog' = horse, 'foreign X' / 'X-like native analog'); Witkowski & Brown 1983 (marking reversals); Buck 1949 (A Dictionary of Selected Synonyms in the Principal Indo-European Languages); Haspelmath & Tadmor 2009 (WOLD 'analyzable' words); the generic + specific compounds of Mainland Southeast Asia (Thai nók-X 'bird-X', plaa-X 'fish-X', tôn-X 'tree-X'; Malay pohon X, burung X; Mandarin song-shu 'pine-tree', li-yu 'carp-fish'; Enfield 2003, Bisang 1999) and English reindeer < Old Norse hreinn + deer.
# version: hand-authored 2026-11-04 (procedural-language lane, compounds and shifts round)
# licence: original text for this repository (no third-party data copied); cite the works above when using it.

# CLICS3: at load time lexicon.py joins each (target, head) and (target, modifier) pair with data/clics_edges.tsv; a pair CLICS3 also attests as a colexification in >= 3 families (BARK/SKIN 49, MILK/BREAST 26, MOON/SUN 18 ...) adds family count / 10 to the weight (a motivated compound is often a colexification too).

# columns: target = the concept named; head = the semantic category the target is a kind (or a part) of: 'tree SKIN' for bark, 'day EYE' for sun, 'mountain ROAD' for a pass, 'woman CHILD' for a girl; modifier = the word that says which one ('SELF' = the target's own current word: a generic + specific renewal, Thai plaa-X, English rein-deer); weight = typicality 1 (attested, uncommon) .. 3 (common across families); example = one or two real cases (romanized) or the source.

# Only these recipes make compounds (lexicon.compound); a target with no row is renewed by derivation, shift, a loan or a fresh root instead. Elaborations (lexicon.ELABORATIONS: MILK + SOUR = soured milk) and function-word reinforcement (data/derivations.tsv 'reinforce' rows) are separate tables.

column5: 'tree skin': Swahili ganda la mti; Urban 2012 (bark/skin colexified in 49 CLICS families)
'bird hair': Tok Pisin gras bilong pisin, Quechua; Urban 2012
'head grass': Tok Pisin gras bilong het; Urban 2012 (hair ~ grass)
'breast water': Urban 2012 (milk ~ breast colexified in 26 CLICS families)
'tree child': Hausa dan itace 'child of tree' = fruit; Urban 2012
'eye of day': Malay mata hari, widely in Austronesian; Urban 2012
'night sun': Ojibwe dibik-giizis, Lakota hanhepi wi
'big wind': Tok Pisin bikpela win; Japanese o-kaze
'big water': Tok Pisin bikpela wara; Algonquian kichi- 'great' + water
'eye of water': Arabic 'ayn al-ma', Hebrew 'ayin, Persian cheshme, Turkish goz; Urban 2012
'flowing water': Urban 2012 (river ~ water colexified in 38 CLICS families)
'little mountain': Urban 2012 (hill ~ mountain colexified in 20 CLICS families)
'house of the dead': Latin domus aeterna; Urban 2012
'sun comes': Malay matahari terbit 'sun emerges'; Urban 2012
'sun falls': Malay matahari terbenam 'sun sinks'; English sundown
'where the sun comes out': Hebrew mizrah 'rising'; Austronesian 'sun rises'
'where the sun falls': Hebrew ma'arav, Arabic gharb 'setting'; English sundown
'left hand (facing sunrise)': Old Irish tuaisceart, Hebrew smol 'left; north'
'right hand (facing sunrise)': Sanskrit daksina, Hebrew yamin, Arabic yaman 'right; south'
'river head': English headwaters; Malay hulu 'head; upstream'
'big man': Tok Pisin bikman, Melanesian big-man; Sumerian lugal 'big man' = king
'woman child': Japanese onna-no-ko, Tok Pisin pikinini meri
'man child': Japanese otoko-no-ko, Tok Pisin pikinini man
'man child': Japanese otoko-no-ko; Tok Pisin pikinini man
'big mother': German Grossmutter, French grand-mere, Hungarian nagyanya
'big father': German Grossvater, French grand-pere, Hungarian nagyapa
'little father': Swahili baba mdogo (father's younger brother)
'little mother': Swahili mama mdogo (mother's younger sister)
'house man': English husband < Old Norse hus-bondi 'house dweller'
'dog child': Japanese ko-inu, Tok Pisin pikinini dog
'one from ten': Latin un-de-viginti (19), Ainu sinepesan
'big dog': Cree mistatim, Lakota sunka wakan 'holy dog'; Brown 1999
'big deer': Brown 1999 (introduced animals named after native ones)
'little deer': Brown 1999 (Tzeltal tunim chij 'cotton deer' = sheep)
'big deer': Brown 1999 (introduced and large animals named after native ones)
'earth fruit': French pomme de terre, German Erdapfel, Dutch aardappel 'earth apple'
'earth nut': English earthnut / groundnut, German Erdnuss
'white metal': Latin plumbum album 'white lead' = tin
